# Baja Mineral Explorer

> A reproducible geospatial data pipeline for mineral-exploration field planning.
> Ingests public geological, satellite, elevation, and mine-inventory data;
> validates and normalizes coordinates; ranks candidate targets; produces
> GPS-ready field packages. Public demo, no login.
> This desk study organizes incomplete public evidence into explicit,
> field-testable hypotheses — not a discovery claim.

## What this site is
An independent desk-study atlas combining:
- Sentinel-2 2020 cloudless *viewing* composite (rendered RGB; visual consistency, not analysis-ready reflectance; S2 bands natively 4×10 m / 6×20 m / 3×60 m; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
- Esri World Imagery viewing tiles (rendered Web-Mercator display scale: z17 ≈1.03, z18 ≈0.52 m/px at sheet latitude — not sensor GSD; research use)
- SRTM elevation (~30 m native, resampled to a 10 m working grid — resampling adds no terrain detail; public domain) for slope/aspect/hillshade
- SGM Carta Geológico-Minera El Aguajito H11-B85, 1:50,000 (2009) geology + 14-workings inventory

## Key coordinates
- T1 Arroyo San Isidro: 29.903605, -115.383656 (prospectivity 5.3/10, feasibility 6.0/10 — shown separately, not a probability) — pale patches on an N–S relay drainage, ~332 m
- T2 Cerro la Turquesa: 30.048522, -115.236173 (prospectivity 7.2/10, feasibility 4.3/10, highest prospectivity under the current model) — km-scale pale surface ~1 km W, NE–SW lineament ~1 km E, turquoise-mining toponym, 740 m hill
- T3 Cerro la Palmita: 30.025725, -115.286885 (prospectivity 5.7/10, feasibility 5.7/10) — ridge between T1/T2, steepest terrain (30% area >15° slope), 800 m
- Documented Cu–Fe belt (La Turquesa zona mineralizada, SGM 2009): 14 abandoned workings between 30.05–30.15° N, 115.34–115.52° W (El Cardonal — documented turquoise; San Martín — chrysocolla/azurite/malachite; La Turquesa core; El Hormiguero; La Bonita; 5 Minas; El Sacrificio; Josefina; Santa Martha; Santa Lucía; La Víbora; El Moro)
- No field survey, geochemistry, spectroscopy, or drilling has validated the three candidate targets.

## Method
Per coordinate the pipeline computes an unvalidated RGB visual-screening heuristic (B/R ratio — prioritization aid, not a mineral identifier), HSV surface classes, and DEM-working-grid slope, aspect, hillshade and drainage transects, then cross-references the SGM 1:50,000 sheet. Full-band mode (free Earthdata login) adds NDVI, ferric-iron, clay and carbonate indices at 30 m. Anything spectral needs validation with analysis-ready data and field observation. Google/Bing data is used only via official APIs (Earth Engine, Bing Maps Imagery API); no tile-server scraping. Scoring: published weights (geology 20, workings 15, spectral 15, structure 15, exposure 10, access 10, water/regulatory 15) in src/scores.py; deterministic and CI-enforced.

## Data downloads
- /maps/PIN_POINTS.csv + /maps/PIN_POINTS.geojson — all 36 field pins (unique v2 IDs, EPSG:4326, provenance; schema: schemas/pins.schema.json)
- /maps/mine_inventory_elaguajito.csv + .geojson — 14 documented SGM workings
- /maps/*.jpg — pin sheets, 0.52 m/px rendered pale-mass detail, 4×4 km field sheets, corridor overview (each with a ~5%-weight *-preview.webp)
- Public demo (#demo): any coordinate → distances/bearings + JSON/GeoJSON + field-package download, 5 analyses/visitor (browser-local)

## Disclaimers
Desk study only — not investment, drilling, or legal advice. Mexican mining is
governed by the Ley Minera (2023 reform): concessions only by public tender,
prohibited in ANPs and water-stressed zones, prior consultation required.
Not affiliated with SGM, CONAGUA, or the Government of Mexico.

## Languages
English (default), Spanish (?lang=es), Chinese (?lang=zh), Russian (?lang=ru). EN reflects the 2026-09 review pass; other locales may lag (translations pending).
